question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

A good lawyer / always looks in the / case before he / attends court.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. always looks in the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the wrong phrasal verb / preposition. To examine or investigate a matter, the correct phrasal verb is "look into", not "look in". Hence it should be "always looks into the case".

◦ Correct sentence: A good lawyer always looks into the case before he attends court.

• "Look in" (without an object) means to make a short visit; "look into" means to investigate — the context here is investigation, so "into" is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "A good lawyer" — correct (subject).

• "case before he" — correct.

• "attends court" — correct (present simple for a habitual action).

NOTE

• Important phrasal verbs of "look" for SSC:

◦ look into = investigate; look after = take care of; look for = search; look up to = respect; look down on = despise; look up = search for information (dictionary); look forward to = await eagerly; look over = examine quickly.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

On the back foot
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. At a disadvantage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "on the back foot" means to be at a disadvantage, on the defensive, or forced to react rather than act. (रक्षात्मक स्थिति में / नुकसानदेह स्थिति में)

◦ Example: The sudden questions from the reporters put the minister on the back foot.

• It originates from cricket, where a batsman playing "on the back foot" is defending rather than attacking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "In a relaxed state", Option 2 "Situated farther away" and Option 4 "In a hurry" do not convey the sense of being on the defensive.

NOTE

• Opposite idiom: "on the front foot" = in a confident, attacking or advantageous position.

• Related idioms of difficulty: "in a tight corner", "on the ropes", "with one's back to the wall".

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

According to Greek mythology, Sipylus is holier city of Lydia.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the holiest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Describing one city as the most sacred among all the cities "of Lydia" requires the superlative degree with the definite article "the" — "the holiest city of Lydia".

◦ Correct: According to Greek mythology, Sipylus is the holiest city of Lydia.

• Adjectives ending in a consonant + "y" form the superlative by changing "y" to "i" and adding "-est": holy → holiest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "most holiest" is a double superlative (both "most" and "-est") — always incorrect.

• Option 3 "the holier" is comparative, used to compare only two things (with "than").

• Option 4 "most holy" is grammatically possible but lacks the required article "the" before it in this structure.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: holy – holier – holiest. The definite article "the" almost always precedes a superlative (the tallest, the best, the holiest).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Before the internet was available on mobile, I read often books for entertainment and information.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. I read often books.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is one of word order (misplaced adverb of frequency). Adverbs of frequency such as "often" are placed before the main verb, not between the verb and its object.

◦ Correct: Before the internet was available on mobile, I often read books for entertainment and information.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Before the internet", "was available on mobile" and "for entertainment and information" are all correct.

NOTE

• Placement of adverbs of frequency (always, often, usually, sometimes, never, rarely, seldom):

◦ Before the main verb — "She often visits us."

◦ After the verb "to be" — "He is often late."

◦ Between the auxiliary and the main verb — "I have often thought about it".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Gloomy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Dismal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gloomy" means dark, dull and depressing; feeling or causing sadness. (उदास / निराशाजनक)

• Its closest synonym is "dismal", meaning depressing, dreary and cheerless.

◦ Example: The weather was gloomy/dismal, with grey clouds all day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Sticky" (adhesive) and Option 2 "Vain" (conceited / useless) are unrelated.

• Option 4 "Buoyant" (cheerful / able to float) is an antonym of gloomy.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gloomy: dismal, dreary, melancholy, morose, sombre, bleak.

• Antonyms of gloomy: cheerful, bright, buoyant, jovial, sunny.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error.

They decided to / start their journey / towards the hills / in midnight.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. in midnight.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct preposition with "midnight", "noon", "night", "dawn" and "dusk" is "at", not "in". Hence it should be "at midnight".

◦ Correct: They decided to start their journey towards the hills at midnight.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "They decided to", "start their journey" and "towards the hills" are all correct.

NOTE

• Prepositions of time — quick rules for SSC:

◦ at — for precise points: at midnight, at noon, at 5 o'clock, at dawn, at night.

◦ on — for days and dates: on Monday, on 15 August.

◦ in — for longer periods: in the morning, in July, in 2024, in winter.

◦ (Exception: we say "at night" but "in the morning/afternoon/evening".)

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Predicament
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Solution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "predicament" is a difficult, unpleasant or embarrassing situation from which it is hard to escape. (कठिन परिस्थिति / दुविधा)

• Its antonym is "solution" — the means of solving a problem or difficulty.

◦ Example: He found himself in a real predicament when he lost his passport abroad.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Docile" (obedient, easy to manage) is unrelated.

• Option 3 "Mess" (a difficult, untidy situation) is a synonym of predicament, not an antonym.

• Option 4 "Redeem" (to make up for / recover) is a verb and does not fit.

NOTE

• Synonyms of predicament: dilemma, plight, quandary, fix, mess, tight spot.

• Antonyms: solution, remedy, resolution, advantage.

question:
Select the most appropriate superlative adjective form to fill in the blanks.

What's ___ book you've ever read?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the most interesting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "you've ever read" implies a comparison with all the books one has ever read, so the superlative degree is required. As "interesting" is a long (three-syllable) adjective, its superlative is formed with "the most" — "the most interesting".

◦ Correct: What's the most interesting book you've ever read?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "interesting" (positive) and Option 4 "the interesting" lack the superlative sense.

• Option 3 "more interesting" is the comparative, used only for comparing two things (with "than").

NOTE

• Forming degrees of long adjectives (2+ syllables): use "more" (comparative) and "the most" (superlative) — e.g., beautiful – more beautiful – the most beautiful.

• The structure "the + superlative + ... (that) you have ever + past participle" is very common (the best film I've ever seen).

question:
Select the most appropriate present tense form of the verb to fill in the blank.

_______ they like sweets?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Do.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "They" is a plural pronoun, so in the simple present tense an interrogative sentence begins with the auxiliary "Do" — "Do they like sweets?"

◦ Rule: Do + plural subject (I/you/we/they) + base verb; Does + singular subject (he/she/it) + base verb.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "Does" is used with third person singular subjects (he/she/it), not "they".

• Option 2 "Had" and Option 3 "Has" are past/perfect forms and do not fit the required present tense.

NOTE

• Subject–auxiliary agreement in the simple present:

◦ Do — I, you, we, they → "Do you play?"

◦ Does — he, she, it → "Does she play?"

• After "does", the main verb takes no -s ("Does she like?", not "likes").

question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank.

We __________ to follow the traffic rules.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ought.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt word is "ought". "Ought to" is a modal verb used to express moral obligation, duty or advice — "We ought to follow the traffic rules." (चाहिए / कर्तव्य)

◦ Example: You ought to respect your elders.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "aut", 2 "aught" and 4 "oght" are wrong here — "aught" is an archaic word meaning "anything", and "aut"/"oght" are not standard words.

NOTE

• "Ought to" always takes the base form of the verb (ought to go, ought to follow).

• Modals of obligation/advice: must, should, ought to, have to, had better — all express duty or advice with varying strength.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Obsequious
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Obstinate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Obsequious" means excessively obedient, servile or eager to please/flatter. (चापलूस / अत्यधिक आज्ञाकारी)

• Its antonym is "obstinate", meaning stubborn and unwilling to yield or obey.

◦ Example: The obsequious waiter kept bowing to every customer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Ordained" (officially appointed / decreed) is unrelated.

• Option 2 "Obliterate" (to destroy completely) is a verb and unrelated.

• Option 3 "Ostracised" (excluded/banished from a group) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of obsequious: servile, fawning, sycophantic, submissive, cringing.

• Antonyms: obstinate, assertive, domineering, independent.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word.

The sink is clogged due to solid materials.
option_3: A large fixed container to wash hands or utensils
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. A large fixed container to wash hands or utensils.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As a noun, a "sink" is a fixed basin, usually in a kitchen or bathroom, with a water supply and drain, used for washing hands, dishes or utensils. (सिंक / बेसिन)

◦ Example: She washed the plates in the kitchen sink.

• "Clogged" (blocked) confirms it refers to the basin whose drain is blocked by solid material.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a pipeline" and Option 2 "a container which holds water" are inaccurate descriptions.

• Option 4 "to drown in water" is the verb sense of "sink" (to go under water), which does not fit "The sink is clogged".

NOTE

• "Sink" as a verb means to go down/below the surface (the ship sank). As a noun it is the washing basin. Context decides the meaning.

question:
Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank meaningfully.

The _______ on the wall was beautifully painted.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. picture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correctly spelt word is "picture", meaning a painting, drawing or photograph. (चित्र / तस्वीर)

◦ Example: There is a beautiful picture of the Taj Mahal in our classroom.

• Spelling key: PIC + TURE (ends in "-ture", like nature, future, culture).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "pictur", 3 "picter" and 4 "pickchure" are all misspellings.

NOTE

• Many English nouns end in "-ture": picture, nature, future, culture, furniture, adventure, temperature, agriculture. Remember the "-ture" ending.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Despite his initial __________, he eventually agreed to join the team.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. reluctance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The connector "Despite" signals a contrast: something opposed his final agreement to join. "Reluctance" (unwillingness or hesitation) provides that contrast — he was unwilling at first but agreed in the end. (अनिच्छा / हिचकिचाहट)

◦ Correct sense: Despite his initial reluctance, he eventually agreed to join.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "enthusiasm" and Option 3 "determination" would not contrast with agreeing to join (no contradiction), so "despite" would be illogical.

• Option 4 "compassion" (sympathy) is unrelated to the decision to join.

NOTE

• Contrast connectors — despite / in spite of + noun; although / though / even though + clause. They introduce an idea opposite to the main statement.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Industrialisation gives even the least talented person a chance to __________ his livelihood.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Earn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The collocation "earn a/one's livelihood" means to make a living / to earn money to support oneself. Hence "a chance to earn his livelihood." (जीविका कमाना)

◦ Example: He works hard to earn his livelihood and support his family.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Live" would need a different structure ("earn a living"/"make a living"); "live his livelihood" is not idiomatic.

• Options 2 "Give" and 4 "Break" do not collocate with "livelihood".

NOTE

• Common collocations with "livelihood": earn/make/gain a livelihood, a source of livelihood, a means of livelihood.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

A grand function was organised to honour the person who had died for a noble cause.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. martyr.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "martyr" is a person who dies or suffers greatly for a noble cause, belief or country. (शहीद / बलिदानी)

◦ Example: Bhagat Singh is remembered as a martyr of India's freedom struggle.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "volunteer" — a person who offers to do something without being paid or forced.

• Option 3 "prophet" — a person who is believed to be a messenger of God / one who foretells the future.

• Option 4 "philanthropist" — a person who helps others, especially by donating money to good causes.

NOTE

• More one-word substitutes for SSC: patriot (one who loves his country), mercenary (a soldier who fights for money), fanatic (one filled with excessive zeal), altruist (one who works for others' welfare).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The investigating team smelled a __________ in the suspect's defence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. rat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to smell a rat" means to suspect that something is wrong, deceitful or dishonest. It fits the context of an investigating team growing suspicious of a suspect's defence. (गड़बड़ी का संदेह होना)

◦ Example: When the accounts didn't match, the auditor smelled a rat.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "smell a cat/bat/dog" are not valid English idioms; only "smell a rat" carries the meaning of suspicion.

NOTE

• Related idioms of suspicion/deceit: "something fishy", "a fly in the ointment", "to see through someone", "a wolf in sheep's clothing".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Inadvertant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inadvertant" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Inadvertent", meaning unintentional or accidental; not done on purpose. (अनजाने में / अनवधानतावश)

◦ Example: An inadvertent error in the form delayed his application.

• Spelling key: IN + AD + VER + TENT — the ending is "-ent", not "-ant".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Synchronous" (happening at the same time), "Effeminate" (having womanly qualities) and "Blatant" (very obvious / shameless) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• The "-ent / -ant" ending is a common spelling trap. Correctly spelt "-ent" words: inadvertent, independent, consistent, persistent, different, competent. "-ant" words: important, relevant, dominant, tolerant.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the highlighted word(s) in the given sentence.

Mr. Wilson is elder than he looks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. older than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Elder" is used only attributively (before a noun) and within a family (my elder brother); it is never followed by "than". For general comparisons of age we use "older than".

◦ Correct: Mr. Wilson is older than he looks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "older then" is wrong — "then" (time) must be "than" (comparison).

• Options 2 "elder to" and 3 "elder for" use wrong prepositions; "elder" is not used with "than/to/for" in this way.

NOTE

• Elder/eldest — only for people, especially family, used before a noun (my eldest son). Older/oldest — for people and things, and used with "than" (older than me). Do not confuse "than" (comparison) with "then" (time).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Awsome.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Awsome" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Awesome", meaning extremely impressive, or causing awe/admiration. (अद्भुत / विस्मयकारी)

◦ Example: The view from the mountain top was truly awesome.

• Spelling key: AWE + SOME — it keeps the "e" of "awe".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Awful", "Bitter" and "Barren" are all correctly spelt.

• Note the contrast: "awful" (very bad / unpleasant) drops the "e" of awe, but "awesome" (wonderful) keeps it.

NOTE

• Words from "awe": awe (noun), awesome (wonderful), awful (very bad), awestruck (filled with awe). Watch the "e" — awEsome keeps it, awful does not.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Opera refers (1)_______ a dramatic art form, originating in Europe, in which the emotional content (2)_______ conveyed to the audience as much through music, both vocal and instrumental, as it is through the lyrics. (3)_______ contrast, in musical theatre an actor's dramatic performance is primary, and the music (4)_______ a lesser role. The drama in opera is (5)_______ using the primary elements of theatre such as scenery, costumes and acting.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "refer" takes the preposition "to" when it means "to denote / to be about". Hence "Opera refers to a dramatic art form ...". (संदर्भित करना)

◦ Example: The term "monsoon" refers to a seasonal wind.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Refer on/for/with" are all incorrect prepositions with the verb "refer".

NOTE

• Verb + preposition collocations for SSC: refer to, listen to, belong to, depend on, insist on, consist of, deal with, agree with.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Opera refers (1)_______ a dramatic art form, originating in Europe, in which the emotional content (2)_______ conveyed to the audience as much through music, both vocal and instrumental, as it is through the lyrics. (3)_______ contrast, in musical theatre an actor's dramatic performance is primary, and the music (4)_______ a lesser role. The drama in opera is (5)_______ using the primary elements of theatre such as scenery, costumes and acting.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. is.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "the emotional content" is singular (an uncountable noun), and the sentence is a general present truth in the passive voice, so the singular verb "is" is correct — "the emotional content is conveyed to the audience".

◦ The passive structure here is: is + past participle (is conveyed).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "were" (past plural) and 4 "are" (present plural) do not agree with the singular subject "content".

• Option 3 "are being" is plural and continuous — wrong number and wrong aspect for a general truth.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: uncountable nouns (content, information, water, advice) take a singular verb (is/was), not plural.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Opera refers (1)_______ a dramatic art form, originating in Europe, in which the emotional content (2)_______ conveyed to the audience as much through music, both vocal and instrumental, as it is through the lyrics. (3)_______ contrast, in musical theatre an actor's dramatic performance is primary, and the music (4)_______ a lesser role. The drama in opera is (5)_______ using the primary elements of theatre such as scenery, costumes and acting.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. In.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed linking phrase is "In contrast", used to introduce an idea that is opposite to what was said before. Here it contrasts opera (where music is central) with musical theatre (where acting is primary). (इसके विपरीत)

◦ Example: John is very tall. In contrast, his brother is quite short.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "For contrast", "Under contrast" and "Beside contrast" are not standard linking phrases.

NOTE

• Contrast connectors: in contrast, on the contrary, on the other hand, conversely, whereas, while. ("In contrast to" + noun; "In contrast," at the start of a sentence.)

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Opera refers (1)_______ a dramatic art form, originating in Europe, in which the emotional content (2)_______ conveyed to the audience as much through music, both vocal and instrumental, as it is through the lyrics. (3)_______ contrast, in musical theatre an actor's dramatic performance is primary, and the music (4)_______ a lesser role. The drama in opera is (5)_______ using the primary elements of theatre such as scenery, costumes and acting.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. plays.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "the music" is third person singular and the sentence is in the simple present tense, so the verb takes "-s" → "the music plays a lesser role". The idiom "to play a role" means to have a part or function.

◦ Example: Diet plays an important role in good health.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "playing" and Option 3 "play" do not agree with the singular subject in the simple present.

• Option 4 "played" (past tense) breaks the present-tense sequence of the passage.

NOTE

• Simple present, third person singular: verb + s/es (he plays, she goes, it works). Common collocation: "play a role / play a part" in something.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Opera refers (1)_______ a dramatic art form, originating in Europe, in which the emotional content (2)_______ conveyed to the audience as much through music, both vocal and instrumental, as it is through the lyrics. (3)_______ contrast, in musical theatre an actor's dramatic performance is primary, and the music (4)_______ a lesser role. The drama in opera is (5)_______ using the primary elements of theatre such as scenery, costumes and acting.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. presented.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "The drama in opera is ___ using ..." requires the passive voice — "is + past participle". The past participle of "present" is "presented", giving "The drama in opera is presented using the primary elements of theatre".

◦ Passive: is/am/are + V3 (past participle).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "presenting" (present participle) would make it active, but there is no active agent here.

• Option 3 "being present" (present = adjective "in attendance") changes the meaning entirely.

• Option 4 "present" (base form) does not fit after "is".

NOTE

• Passive voice = form of "be" + past participle (V3). It is used when the focus is on the action/receiver rather than the doer, as in "The drama is presented", "The letter was written" and "The house is being built".
